decision: Use a bounded process-per-call qrexec controller that launches a detached local synthetic executor with durable per-run state; stop is state-based rather than PID-signal-based.
winner: bounded detached executor + durable state cancellation

correctness.reason: qrexec services are process-per-call, so start must outlive the request while stop must find the same execution later. The state file preserves that lifecycle without changing coordinator semantics.

security_robustness.preferred: fixed synthetic CPU loop + state-based cancellation + strict validation
security_robustness.reason: Only timing data is accepted. Stop marks the exact run/workload state as stopped and the executor observes that state, avoiding process.kill on a PID that could theoretically have been recycled after an executor crash.

latency_resources_regression.preferred: one detached executor per active worker calibration
latency_resources_regression.reason: No daemon, database, network listener, arbitrary command execution, or coordinator mutation is added. State polling adds only a few milliseconds of local filesystem overhead and no extra qrexec round trip.

alternatives.approach: keep workload in the qrexec service process
alternatives.rejectedBecause: the start call would block for the calibration duration and prevent concurrent resource sampling
adds lifecycle, credential, listening-surface, and resource complexity before real Qubes qualification

alternatives.approach: signal the persisted executor PID on stop
alternatives.rejectedBecause: a stale state file plus PID reuse could signal an unrelated process; state cancellation removes that class of failure
unnecessary command-execution authority and unacceptable security/regression surface

qaGates: reject unsafe names, overlong workloads, duplicate missions, and schedule entries outside duration
persist start state before spawning and reject duplicate active starts
stop is idempotent and state-based; it never signals a PID
repeated stop preserves the original stop timestamp
executor remains duration-bounded even if stop is never called
service test is present in syntax/full/local/hosted distributed-fault QA
failuresLessons: A process-per-call qrexec service cannot represent a running workload with in-memory state.
The first design used PID signalling; independent robustness review rejected it because PID reuse can turn stale state into cross-process impact.
Resource calibration must not gain arbitrary-code execution just to produce load; the workload language stays timing-only and synthetic.
The workload executor must remain bounded even if stop is never called, so duration is enforced inside the executor.
safety: Synthetic defensive calibration only. No financial transactions, payment data, external side effects, arbitrary shell commands, or weakened security controls.
